Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. The example uses the **gcloud CLI** (the easiest way to interact with the Compute Engine API) and also shows the equivalent **REST API call** if you prefer to call the API directly. > ⚠️ **Prerequisites** > * You must have a Google Cloud project with billing enabled. > * The **Compute Engine API** must be enabled for that project. > * You must have the **gcloud SDK** installed and authenticated (`gcloud auth login`). > * The **GPU quota** for your project must allow at least one RTX A6000 in the zone you choose. > * The **GPU driver** will be installed automatically by the image’s startup script. --- ## 1. Using the gcloud CLI ```bash # 1️⃣ Set the project and zone you want to use PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project" # <-- replace with your project ID ZONE="us-central1-a" # <-- pick a zone that supports RTX A6000 # 2️⃣ Create a machine type that can host a GPU # The default machine types (e.g., n1-standard-8) are fine. MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" # 3️⃣ Pick an image that already has the GPU drivers pre‑installed # The official NVIDIA image includes the drivers and the CUDA toolkit. IMAGE_PROJECT="nvidia-cloud" IMAGE_FAMILY="nvidia-ubuntu-2004" # 4️⃣ Name of the instance INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo" # 5️⃣ Create the instance gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE_NAME" \ --project="$PROJECT_ID" \ --zone="$ZONE" \ --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \ --image-project="$IMAGE_PROJECT" \ --image-family="$IMAGE_FAMILY" \ --boot-disk-size=100GB \ --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \ --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \ --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \ --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \ --accelerator type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \ --tags=http-server,https-server \ --network-interface=network-tier=PREMIUM,subnet=default \ --reservation-affinity=any ``` ### What the command does | Step | What happens | |------|--------------| | 1 | Sets the project and zone. | | 2 | Uses a standard machine type that can host GPUs. | | 3 | Uses the official NVIDIA image family `nvidia-ubuntu-2004`, which contains Ubuntu 20.04 LTS plus the NVIDIA driver and CUDA toolkit. | | 4 | Gives the instance a friendly name. | | 5 | Creates the instance with:
• 100 GB SSD boot disk
• 1 RTX A6000 GPU
• Automatic driver installation via the image’s startup script
• HTTP/HTTPS firewall rules
• Premium network tier | > **Tip**: If you want a different machine type (e.g., more CPUs or memory), just change `MACHINE_TYPE`. > **Tip**: If you need a different zone, make sure that zone supports the GPU type you want. --- ## 2. Equivalent REST API Call If you prefer to call the Compute Engine REST API directly (e.g., from a script or a custom application), here’s the `curl` command that does the same thing: ```bash # 1️⃣ Set variables PROJECT_ID="my-gcp-project" ZONE="us-central1-a" INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-demo" MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8" IMAGE_PROJECT="nvidia-cloud" IMAGE_FAMILY="nvidia-ubuntu-2004" # 2️⃣ Get the full machine type URL MACHINE_TYPE_URL="https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE" # 3️⃣ Get the latest image from the family IMAGE_RESPONSE=$(curl -s "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY") IMAGE_SELF_LINK=$(echo "$IMAGE_RESPONSE" | jq -r '.selfLink') # 4️⃣ Build the JSON body read -r -d '' INSTANCE_BODY < **Note**: The `curl` example uses `jq` to parse JSON. If you don’t have `jq`, you can manually replace the `sourceImage` field with the image’s self‑link. --- ## 3. After the Instance Is Created Once the instance is running, you can SSH into it: ```bash gcloud compute ssh "$INSTANCE_NAME" --zone="$ZONE" ``` Inside the instance, verify the GPU is visible: ```bash nvidia-smi ``` You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version and CUDA version. --- ## 4. Quick Checklist | ✅ | Item | |----|------| | ✅ | Project ID set | | ✅ | Zone supports RTX A6000 | | ✅ | Compute Engine API enabled | | ✅ | GPU quota available | | ✅ | gcloud SDK installed & authenticated | | ✅ | Image family `nvidia-ubuntu-2004` used | | ✅ | `--accelerator` flag set to `nvidia-tesla-a6000` | | ✅ | `--metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh` (optional) | --- ### Final Thoughts * The **official NVIDIA image** (`nvidia-cloud/nvidia-ubuntu-2004`) takes care of installing the correct driver and CUDA toolkit, so you don’t have to manually install anything. * If you need a different CUDA version, you can either use a different image family (e.g., `nvidia-ubuntu-2004-cuda-11-8`) or add a custom startup script that installs the CUDA toolkit after the instance boots. * For production workloads, consider using **managed instance groups** or **autoscaling** if you plan to run many GPU instances. Happy GPU computing! 🚀
